title: tri-sdk: stream resume + preflight auth handshake + ergonomic streaming builders
author: Maya Chen
commits: feat(sdk): add preflight auth handshake for streaming connections
perf(stream): idempotent stream resume token + server-side ack handling
refactor(python): expose AsyncStreamBuilder and default backoff profiles
feat(go): streaming iterator ergonomics and context-aware token refresh
tests: add e2e stream resume tests across python/ts/go
chore: bump sdks python->1.4.3 ts->2.0.0 go->0.9.1 and changelogs
description: Motivation: We continue to see customer reports and internal test flakes where long-running streaming calls fail mid-stream with a 401/403 when tokens rotate or when transient network blips occur. Existing SDK behavior either kills the stream or requires heavy user-side glue to resume. This PR implements a three-part change for parity across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs: 1) a lightweight preflight auth handshake on stream open so the client and server can agree on a token-refresh strategy and initial resume id; 2) an idempotent stream-resume token and server ack protocol (protocol described in pkg/api/stream/protocol.md) allowing clients to reconnect and request content after the last acked chunk; 3) ergonomic streaming builders / iterators so application code can resume the stream with minimal plumbing. The description below describes the non-obvious implementation details, test coverage, and upgrade notes.
protocol_summary: The stream now begins with a preflight control frame: { type: "preflight", client_resume_id, token_version }. The server responds with { type: "preflight_ack", server_resume_id, accepted_token_version }. During normal streaming, server emits periodic ack markers: { type: "ack", server_resume_id, offset }. On reconnect clients present the last seen server_resume_id and offset. The server will replay from the safe offset or return a non-retryable error if the session window has expired.
python_changes:
Added AsyncStreamBuilder in sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py which wraps the websocket/http2 stream and exposes an async for interface. Default backoff shapes were adjusted to jittered-exponential with max 30s and default attempts=6. Token refresh hook integrated: if a 401 occurs mid-stream the builder attempts a non-blocking refresh and performs a resume handshake. Example usage in docs: async for chunk in client.stream.create_stream(request, resume_policy="auto"):
    handle(chunk)
typescript_changes: Added ReadableStream wrapper and pipeTo helper in sdk/typescript/src/stream/index.ts. New StreamConfig exposes resumePolicy and authPreflight options. We export a node-friendly stream.Readable and browser ReadableStream interop. Tests added that run in node and headless chromium to validate reconnects and backpressure handling.
go_changes: Added iterator-style StreamNext(ctx) in sdk/go/stream/client.go that returns (chunk, resumeToken, err). Token refresh is context-aware; client can inject a RefreshTokenFunc. Tests added to simulate mid-stream 401 and validate resume works without duplicate delivery.
tests_and_ci: Added cross-language e2e tests under sdk/*/tests that run against the local stream canary. CI matrix added a 'stream-e2e' job. First pipeline run failed due to flaky timing in the Python reconnect test (timeout=0.5s too low); adjusted timing and retries, rerun succeeded. New tests cover: preflight failure modes, resume within session window, resume after server restart (session window expired), ack idempotency.

notes_for_release: SDKs: python 1.4.3, typescript 2.0.0, go 0.9.1. Highlights: preflight auth handshake for streaming, idempotent resume tokens, ergonomic async/iter interfaces. Migration: users on long-lived streams should migrate to resumePolicy="auto" to benefit from seamless reconnects. See docs/sdks/streaming.md for code samples and protocol details.
release_notes: Added preflight handshake to reduce mid-stream auth failures
Clients can now resume streams without application-level buffering
New ergonomic builders: AsyncStreamBuilder (Python), ReadableStream wrapper (TS), iterator API (Go)
Backoff defaults tightened to reduce overload during mass reconnects
SDK version bumps: Python 1.4.3, TypeScript 2.0.0, Go 0.9.1
upgrade_instructions: 1) Update SDK packages to the new versions. 2) In long-running stream handlers, switch to the provided builders/iterators and set resumePolicy="auto". 3) If you log full stream metadata, update logging config to redact resume tokens. 4) For private deployments, ensure stream session window (config 'stream.session_window_seconds') is set compatibly with server retention (recommended >= 120s).
backwards_compatibility: Clients that do not opt into preflight will continue to work: server accepts an absent preflight and falls back to previous behavior (no resume). The new resume protocol is additive; servers will only require it after a future major version bump.
